title: Regininha's death mobilizes fans and highlights musical journey
seoTitle: Regininha's Death Highlights Her Musical Legacy
subtitle: The singer and songwriter passed away this Tuesday, reigniting interest in her work
excerpt: Regininha, the voice behind "Teletema", died at 81. The news brought to light her career, partnerships, and music's impact on "Véu de Noiva".
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Regininha, the interpreter of the song "Teletema" that marked the telenovela "Véu de Noiva" in 1970, passed away this Tuesday at the age of 81. The news reported by GloboNews generated widespread repercussion, bringing the artist's name back into the news and online searches.

What sparked the return of public attention

The singer's death revived memories of the song that soundtracked the telenovela's romance, as well as recalling her time with groups such as Turma da Pilantragem and the trio Umas e Outras. The fact that the cause of death was not disclosed also fueled readers' curiosity.

Regininha's artistic journey

Born in Rio de Janeiro as Regina Amália Serra de Souza, Regininha began her career in the late 1960s. She joined Turma da Pilantragem between 1968 and 1969 and, the following year, became part of the trio Umas e Outras. Afterward, she pursued a solo career, achieving national prominence.

Relevant partnerships and collaborations

Throughout her professional life, Regininha worked alongside names such as Gilberto Gil, Alceu Valença, Roberto Carlos, Elba Ramalho, Carlos Lyra, Ivan Lins, and Edu Lobo. These collaborations reinforced her presence in the Brazilian musical scene.

Work outside of music

With a degree in Psychology, the singer also worked in the advertising market, producing jingles and doing voice-overs. This experience broadened her repertoire and allowed her to move between different creative fields.

The legacy of the song "Teletema"

"Teletema" was part of the soundtrack of the telenovela "Véu de Noiva", starring Regina Duarte, and became the biggest success of Regininha's career. The melody remains associated with the plot's central romance, keeping the artist's memory alive among new generations of viewers.

With information from Folha de S.Paulo, Jornal Correio.
